messages:
maria: Quick spike result — partial-mask + fuzzy-hash seems promising for request logs. Keeps token counts stable and still obfuscates identifiers.
sam: can you paste the config you used? interested in how the hash is computed.
maria: sure, quick snippet:
```
route: /v1/generate
log_mask: partial_mask
partial_mask.strategy: fuzzy_hash
partial_mask.window: 6
partial_mask.hash_algo: blake2b
partial_mask.salt: <team-salt>
```
sam: nice. so we keep first/last 2 chars and replace middle with hash? what's collision risk for short ids?
maria: yep. we keep prefix/suffix and insert a truncated hash (8 chars). collisions low enough for telemetry purposes. the idea is to allow grouping by same identifier without revealing full value.
tony: question: downstream consumers (analytics, debugging) rely on stable pseudonyms. Are we confident the salt rotation won't break correlation?
maria: good catch. plan is: per-tenant salt stored in KMS, rotation documented and a migration path for analytics (recompute on ingest if old salt retained for N days).
jun: how does this impact embeddings leakage? If masked value is fed into embeddings, could models still memorize patterns?
maria: embedding risk is the main open risk. For now we will NOT forward masked identifiers into embeddings or third-party sinks. Masked strings are treated as opaque tokens when producing vectors.
elaine: console UX question: ops want a simple toggle for "masking level" (none / partial_mask / redact). How do we show per-route expected cardinality so they don't enable partial_mask on high-cardinality routes and blow up metrics?
tony: add a small estimator: sample last 5k requests and compute distinct id count and estimated grouping utility. render as "expected pseudonym groups per 10k requests".
maria: agreed. also add a tooltip: "partial_mask preserves grouping but not PII; use redact for GDPR-sensitive routes".
sam: rollout plan? we need a canary and a way for SRE to force full redact if unexpected leak.
maria: proposal: 1) server-side flag per-route, 2) console canary toggle with scope (team/org), 3) remote kill switch in ops console to force redact globally, 4) audit-bot to record any toggles.
elaine: can we wire a justification field when turning off redact? we need an audit trail for compliance.
maria: yes — the toggle flow will require a short reason and optional ticket link.
audit-bot: [auto] policy-change record created by maria at 1749991130: route=/v1/generate, old=redact, new=partial_mask, scope=canary:team-alpha
jun: performance note: partial_mask adds about 0.4ms per request in our benchmark (string ops + blake2b short). batching amortizes it, but cold paths see the hit.
tony: 0.4ms is fine, but watch the tail latency under burst. Can we async-mask in the writer pipeline for non-sensitive downstreams?
maria: yes, async option is possible: write raw to ephemeral buffer, mask before durable store. downside: short window where raw exists in memory/durable buffer. ops/legal may not accept that.
sam: can we do deterministically reversible pseudonymization for debugging with a privileged vault key? i.e. reversible encrypt + audit unseal.
elaine: legal prefers non-reversible for PII unless there's a strict process. reversible option could be gated behind a ticketed audit unseal flow.
jun: telemetry quotas: if we keep grouped ids, metrics cardinality might spike for routes that previously were redacted. need quota alarms.
maria: we'll add a quota-estimator (elaine's estimator) and a preflight that warns if enabling partial_mask would increase cardinality beyond threshold. Also automatic fallback: if metric ingestion rate crosses threshold, auto-switch to redact and notify owners.
tony: who owns the fallback policy? eng-platform? operations?
elaine: eng-platform owns the feature, SRE owns the emergency fallback. implement as config: fallback_policy: {trigger: metric-rate-10k/s, action: revert_to: redact, notify: #oncall}
sam: minor: make sure logs include schema version so older consumers know how to parse pseudonyms.
maria: added to PR. i'll draft the RFC with: threat model (embeddings, key rotation, collisions), console UX mock, canary plan, audit flow, performance numbers.
jun: please include a short runbook for "how to revoke partial masks if a leak is suspected".
maria: will do. planning to open RFC today and request review from legal/compliance and data-protection.
tony: :eyes: ping me when PR is up, i'll review the estimator math.
elaine: I'll prototype the console toggle UX next sprint.
audit-bot: [auto] thread archived for compliance trace at 1749991180
